$comment: NIP-MP conformance fixtures — the shared ingest contract for the relay validator, the Rust event builder, and the TypeScript event builder. Each case carries an UNSIGNED template: consumers sign it with their own test key, because signing fixes the event id and signature and a stored literal would not survive re-serialization. `expect` is the ingest outcome. `reject_rules` lists the validation rules that may fire; an implementation must reject for one of them, so it cannot pass by rejecting for an unrelated reason. This file covers single-event accept/reject only; the client-side fold has its own oracle in NIP-MP.fold-fixtures.json. Spec: docs/nips/NIP-MP.md.

cases.name: valid_minimal
cases.note: Only the identity tag. A project needs nothing but a `d` tag to be a valid addressable container.

cases.name: valid_full
cases.note: Every specified tag present, with two members owned by two different pubkeys — the cross-owner grouping that motivates the kind.

tags: Relay, desktop, and mobile for the platform team.

cases.name: valid_zero_members
cases.note: Zero-member project. Legal at the protocol layer: it is the natural state after removing a final member and carries only bounded metadata.

cases.name: valid_unlisted
cases.note: Explicitly unlisted container. Accepted at ingest; the fold excludes it from listing eligibility, so its member keeps its implicit card.

cases.name: valid_member_cap_boundary
cases.note: Exactly 64 distinct member `a` tags — the cap is inclusive. Paired with `invalid_member_cap_exceeded` to pin the boundary from both sides.

cases.name: valid_same_dtag_two_owners
cases.note: Two members share a repo `d` segment under different owners (the NIP-34 fork case). Identity is the whole coordinate, so these are not duplicates.

cases.name: valid_member_dtag_contains_colon
cases.note: Repo `d` segment contains a colon. The coordinate splits into at most three parts, so the third part is the repo `d` value verbatim — `buzz:infra` here. Splitting on every colon instead would make any repo with a colon in its `d` tag unaddressable by a project.

cases.name: valid_uninterpreted_metadata_values
cases.note: `buzz-channel` is not a UUID and `buzz-visibility` is an unrecognized token. Ingest bounds metadata cardinality and length but does not interpret these values — matching how kind:30617 carries the same two tags. Client-side fallbacks for both are normative in the spec's Metadata interpretation section: an unresolvable channel renders the project without one, and an unrecognized visibility is treated as `listed`.

cases.name: valid_unknown_tag_ignored
cases.note: An unrecognized tag is neither rejected nor interpreted — unknown tags are ignored, not fatal.

cases.name: valid_member_relay_hint
cases.note: Member `a` tag carries NIP-01's optional third element, a relay hint. Ingest validates the tag's arity and the coordinate in element 1, so the hint's content is neither parsed nor a rejection cause; a client MAY use it to resolve an otherwise unavailable member.

cases.name: valid_non_empty_content
cases.note: `content` holds a value. Writers should emit the empty string, but readers and relays must ignore whatever is there — a non-empty `content` is not a rejection cause and carries no semantics.

cases.name: invalid_d_missing
cases.note: No `d` tag. Without one the event collapses into the `(pubkey, 30621, "")` slot and silently last-write-wins over an unrelated project.

cases.name: invalid_d_multiple
cases.note: Two `d` tags. Which one addresses the event is reader-dependent; reject rather than pick.

cases.name: invalid_d_empty
cases.note: Present but empty `d`. Same slot-collapse hazard as a missing `d`.

cases.name: invalid_member_duplicate
cases.note: The same canonical coordinate twice. A signed event cannot be normalized in place, so the relay refuses it rather than store a head every consumer must defensively dedupe.

cases.name: invalid_member_duplicate_differing_relay_hints
cases.note: The same coordinate twice under different relay hints. Duplicate detection compares the coordinate alone, so differing hints do not make these distinct members; a validator that compares whole tag arrays would wrongly accept this.

cases.name: invalid_member_cap_exceeded
cases.note: 65 distinct member `a` tags — one past the inclusive cap of 64.

cases.name: invalid_member_cap_exceeded_by_duplicates
cases.note: 65 member `a` tags naming 33 distinct coordinates. The spec evaluates the cap before the duplicate set is built, so `member-cap` is the required rule even though the event also carries duplicates; a validator that reports `member-duplicate` here has built a set whose size is bounded only by the frame limit.

cases.name: invalid_member_tag_arity_four_elements
cases.note: Member `a` tag carries a fourth element past the relay hint. Its coordinate is valid, so this rejects on tag shape rather than on the coordinate: NIP-01's `a` grammar is two or three elements, and a validator that reads element 1 and ignores the rest would accept unbounded unvalidated data in a position no consumer reads.

cases.name: invalid_member_kind_prefix
cases.note: Coordinate names kind 30618 (repo state) rather than 30617 (repo announcement). A project groups repositories, not their ref state.

cases.name: invalid_member_owner_not_hex
cases.note: Owner segment is 64 characters but not hex.

cases.name: invalid_member_owner_uppercase
cases.note: Owner segment is uppercase hex. `#a` tag matching is byte-exact, so an uppercase head is invisible to the lowercase-coordinate queries every reader issues.

cases.name: invalid_member_owner_wrong_length
cases.note: Owner segment is 63 hex characters.

cases.name: invalid_member_dtag_empty
cases.note: Coordinate has an empty repo `d` segment — it addresses no announceable repository.

cases.name: invalid_member_missing_segment
cases.note: Coordinate has two segments instead of three.

cases.name: invalid_metadata_duplicate_name
cases.note: Two `name` tags. Reader-dependent display name; reject rather than pick.

cases.name: invalid_metadata_duplicate_channel
cases.note: Two `buzz-channel` tags. Which channel the project links to would be reader-dependent.

cases.name: invalid_metadata_name_too_long
cases.note: `name` value exceeds 256 bytes.

cases.name: invalid_metadata_description_too_long
cases.note: `description` value exceeds 2048 bytes.

cases.name: invalid_metadata_channel_too_long
cases.note: `buzz-channel` value exceeds 256 bytes. Paired with `invalid_metadata_visibility_too_long` so each bound is exercised by an event whose other metadata is valid — neither check can hide behind the other's rejection.

cases.name: invalid_metadata_visibility_too_long
cases.note: `buzz-visibility` value exceeds 256 bytes. Ingest does not interpret the token, but it must still bound its length.

cases.name: valid_access_private
cases.note: Buzz access extension: a private project with no invites — readable only by its author.

cases.name: valid_access_private_with_invites
cases.note: Buzz access extension: private project inviting two members; a `p` tag may carry a NIP-01 relay hint.

cases.name: valid_access_public_explicit
cases.note: Buzz access extension: explicit public is identical to the absent-tag default.

cases.name: valid_invite_cap_boundary
cases.note: Exactly invite_cap (256) distinct `p` tags is legal; 257 is not.

cases.name: invalid_access_unknown_value
cases.note: Unlike `buzz-visibility` (display hint, unknown value falls back harmlessly), `buzz-access` is an access-control input: a typo that silently fell open to public would be a privacy leak, so unknown values are rejected.

cases.name: invalid_access_duplicate
cases.note: Two `buzz-access` tags would make the access level itself reader-dependent.

cases.name: invalid_invite_cap_exceeded
cases.note: invite_cap + 1 raw `p` tags. Counted over raw tags before per-tag work, same rationale as member-cap.

cases.name: invalid_invite_tag_arity_four_elements
cases.note: A fourth `p` tag element has no defined meaning; accepting it would park unvalidated data in a position no consumer reads.

cases.name: invalid_invite_not_hex
cases.note: Invite pubkeys must be 64-hex — the read gate compares byte-exact against the authenticated reader's pubkey.

cases.name: invalid_invite_uppercase
cases.note: Lowercase-only for the same byte-exact-matching reason as member coordinates.

cases.name: invalid_invite_duplicate
cases.note: Duplicates are rejected rather than deduped, matching member-duplicate: a relay cannot rewrite tags inside a signed event.
